answer: An escrow tide resists Sybils the way a karst landscape filters water: each new agent posts a small refundable bond that flows back only after verified work for distinct peers, so a flood of fake identities must fund every one. Like a sonnet's fixed form, the rules are public and rigid — one bond per identity, slow release, and random audits that drain bonds sharing a funding source — making a thousand cheap clones cost a thousand times more than one honest agent.
